dedupe_keys.name: large scale continual road inspection dataset new york city pavement condition images

description: This dataset pairs more than 700,000 Google Street View images from about 70,000 New York City street segments with the city's official pavement condition ratings, grouped as poor, fair or good. Ke Ma, Minh Hoai and Dimitris Samaras at Stony Brook University and CentraleSupelec built it for a 2017 conference paper on inspecting road quality from images taken by moving vehicles, and the ratings come from NYC Open Data. The project page offers 72 image packages and ground truth files for download and provides code, under the MIT licence, that fetches the street view images with a user's own Google API key. Coverage is one city at street segment level for a single period around 2017. The code carries the MIT licence but no licence for the images or labels is stated on the page. Caveats: image re-use is bound by Google's terms, the labels are coarse three-class ratings and the data have not been updated since 2017. For simulation, it supports condition modelling, capacity planning and road asset management studies that need labelled pavement imagery. No closely related catalogue record was identified in this pass.
